s0001.literal: Preface: As for the classics and records, they are the subtle purport of the spirit's workings and the achievement of sages and worthies, by which one spans Heaven and Earth, aligns yin and yang, sets right the fundamental norms, and spreads the Way and virtue; when manifest, benevolence suffices to benefit things; when hidden, usefulness suffices for self-cultivation.
s0001.idiomatic: Preface: The classics and records embody the subtle truth of the spirit's workings and the achievement of sages and worthies. Through them one spans Heaven and Earth, aligns yin and yang, sets right the fundamental norms, and spreads the Way and virtue. Revealed, their benevolence suffices to benefit all things; concealed, their usefulness suffices for self-cultivation alone.

s0002.literal: Those who study them will flourish; those who do not study them will decline.
s0002.idiomatic: Those who study them will flourish; those who do not will fall behind.

s0003.literal: When a great enterprise honors them, it brings forth the virtue of profound discernment;
s0003.idiomatic: When a great enterprise honors them, it brings forth the virtue of profound discernment;

s0004.literal: When an ordinary man holds them in mind, he has the weight of kings and dukes.
s0004.idiomatic: When an ordinary man keeps them in mind, he carries the weight of kings and dukes.

s0005.literal: How can kings establish their reputation, transmit their glorious titles, cultivate fine teachings, and transform customs without this Way?
s0005.idiomatic: How can kings establish their reputation, transmit their glorious titles, cultivate fine teachings, and transform customs except through this Way?

s0006.literal: Therefore it is said: A person formed by the teaching of the Odes is gentle and sincere;
s0006.idiomatic: Therefore it is said: A person formed by the teaching of the Odes is gentle and sincere;

s0007.literal: Penetrating in knowledge and far-reaching in vision—this is the teaching of the Documents;
s0007.idiomatic: Penetrating in knowledge and far-reaching in vision—this is the teaching of the Documents;

s0008.literal: Broad in spirit and readily good—this is the teaching of Music;
s0008.idiomatic: Broad in spirit and readily good—this is the teaching of Music;

s0009.literal: Pure, quiet, subtle, and precise—this is the teaching of the Changes;
s0009.idiomatic: Pure, quiet, subtle, and precise—this is the teaching of the Changes;

s0010.literal: Respectful, frugal, dignified, and reverent—this is the teaching of the Rites;
s0010.idiomatic: Respectful, frugal, dignified, and reverent—this is the teaching of the Rites;

s0011.literal: Skilled in linking words and comparing events—this is the teaching of the Spring and Autumn.
s0011.idiomatic: Skilled in linking words and comparing events—this is the teaching of the Spring and Autumn.

s0012.literal: Meeting the needs of the age, substance and ornament alternate in use; one responds with adaptability, and through adaptability one reaches the mean.
s0012.idiomatic: Meeting the needs of the age, substance and ornament alternate in use; one responds with adaptability, and through adaptability one reaches the mean.

s0013.literal: The mean may endure; adaptability may expand.
s0013.idiomatic: The mean may endure; adaptability may expand.

s0014.literal: Its teaching is appropriate; its uses are inexhaustible.
s0014.idiomatic: Its teaching is appropriate; its uses are inexhaustible.

s0015.literal: It is truly the potter's wheel of benevolence and righteousness, the bellows of the Way and virtue.
s0015.idiomatic: It is truly the potter's wheel of benevolence and righteousness, the bellows of the Way and virtue.

s0016.literal: Its function is great; the meaning of acting in accord with the times runs deep—words cannot exhaust praise of it.
s0016.idiomatic: Its function is great, and the meaning of acting in accord with the times runs deep—words cannot exhaust praise of it.

s0017.literal: Therefore it is said: Without haste, yet swift; without going, yet arriving.
s0017.idiomatic: Therefore it is said: Without haste, yet swift; without going, yet arriving.

s0018.literal: That the present should know the past and the future should know the present is what is meant by this.
s0018.idiomatic: That the present should know the past and the future should know the present—this is what is meant.

s0019.literal: Thus when the Great Way was first put into practice, Fu Xi looked down at the tortoise and contemplated its markings and fashioned the hexagrams;
s0019.idiomatic: Thus when the Great Way was first put into practice, Fu Xi looked down at the tortoise, contemplated its markings, and fashioned the hexagrams;

s0020.literal: and when the sage of later times arose, he looked up at the tracks of birds and completed the written script.
s0020.idiomatic: and when the sage of later times arose, he looked up at the tracks of birds and completed the written script.

s0021.literal: Once written contracts were transmitted, knotted cords were abandoned and no longer used;
s0021.idiomatic: Once written contracts were transmitted, knotted cords were abandoned and no longer used;

s0022.literal: once the historiographers were established, the classics and records came into being along with them.
s0022.idiomatic: once the historiographers were established, the classics and records came into being along with them.

s0023.literal: As for the classics and records, the earlier sages, having received the Dragon Chart and grasped the Phoenix Register, and facing south to rule All-under-Heaven, all had historiographers to record words and deeds.
s0023.idiomatic: As for the classics and records, the earlier sages who received the Dragon Chart and grasped the Phoenix Register, and faced south to rule All-under-Heaven, all had historiographers to record words and deeds.

s0024.literal: When the ruler spoke, the left historiographer recorded it; when he acted, the right historiographer recorded it.
s0024.idiomatic: When the ruler spoke, the left historiographer recorded it; when he acted, the right historiographer recorded it.

s0025.literal: Hence the saying "the ruler's every act must be written down"—in this lay censure and encouragement.
s0025.idiomatic: Hence the saying "the ruler's every act must be written down"—in this lay censure and encouragement.

s0026.literal: Looking to earlier records, works such as the Three Fu, Five Canons, Eight Suo, and Nine Mounds belong to this.
s0026.idiomatic: Looking to earlier records, works such as the Three Fu, Five Canons, Eight Suo, and Nine Mounds belong to this category.

s0027.literal: Down through Yin and Zhou, the historiographers were especially complete, recording words and events without omission. Thus what the Rites of Zhou describes: the Grand Historiographer was charged with establishing the six canons, eight laws, and eight regulations of the state, to instruct the king in governance;
s0027.idiomatic: Down through Yin and Zhou, the historiographers were especially complete, recording words and events without omission. Thus what the Rites of Zhou describes: the Grand Historiographer was charged with establishing the six canons, eight laws, and eight regulations of the state, to instruct the king in governance;

s0028.literal: the Minor Historiographer was charged with keeping the records of the states, fixing genealogies, and distinguishing senior and junior lines of descent;
s0028.idiomatic: the Minor Historiographer was charged with keeping the records of the states, fixing genealogies, and distinguishing senior and junior lines of descent;

s0029.literal: the Inner Historiographer was charged with the king's eight powers of command, issuing edicts and keeping duplicate copies;
s0029.idiomatic: the Inner Historiographer was charged with the king's eight powers of command, issuing edicts and keeping duplicate copies;

s0030.literal: the Outer Historiographer was charged with the king's external commands and the records of the four quarters, as well as books of the Three Emperors and Five Thearchs;
s0030.idiomatic: the Outer Historiographer was charged with the king's external commands and the records of the four quarters, as well as books of the Three Emperors and Five Thearchs;

s0031.literal: the Supervising Historiographer was charged with the governing orders for the states, capitals, districts, and myriad people, to assist the Minister of Works.
s0031.idiomatic: the Supervising Historiographer was charged with the governing orders for the states, capitals, districts, and myriad people, to assist the Minister of Works.

s0032.literal: These were the historiographers at the Son of Heaven's court—five in all.
s0032.idiomatic: These were the historiographers at the Son of Heaven's court—five in all.

s0033.literal: Each feudal lord likewise had his own state historiographers, each fulfilling his office.
s0033.idiomatic: Each feudal lord likewise had his own state historiographers, each fulfilling his office.

s0034.literal: Thus in the Zuo Commentary, when Zhao Chuan of Jin assassinated Duke Ling, Grand Historiographer Dong Hu wrote, "Zhao Dun killed his lord," and displayed it in court.
s0034.idiomatic: Thus in the Zuo Commentary, when Zhao Chuan of Jin assassinated Duke Ling, Grand Historiographer Dong Hu wrote, "Zhao Dun killed his lord," and displayed it in court.

s0036.literal: " He replied, "You were chief minister; you fled but did not cross the border, and upon your return you did not punish the villain—if not you, then who?"
s0036.idiomatic: " He replied, "You were chief minister; you fled but did not cross the border, and upon your return you did not punish the villain—if not you, then who?"

s0037.literal: In Qi, Cui Zhu assassinated Duke Zhuang; the Grand Historiographer wrote, "Cui Zhu assassinated his lord," and Cui had him killed.
s0037.idiomatic: In Qi, Cui Zhu assassinated Duke Zhuang; the Grand Historiographer wrote, "Cui Zhu assassinated his lord," and Cui had him killed.

s0038.literal: His younger brother succeeded to the post and wrote the same; two men died.
s0038.idiomatic: His younger brother succeeded to the post and wrote the same; two men died.

s0039.literal: Another younger brother wrote again, and Cui then let the matter go.
s0039.idiomatic: Another younger brother wrote again, and Cui then let the matter go.

s0040.literal: The Southern Historiographer, hearing that the Grand Historiographers had all been killed, took up his bamboo slips and set out, but hearing that it had already been written, he returned.
s0040.idiomatic: The Southern Historiographer, hearing that the Grand Historiographers had all been killed, took up his bamboo slips and set out, but hearing that it had already been written, he returned.

s0041.literal: King Ling of Chu was conversing with Right Intendant Zige when Left Historiographer Yi Xiang hurried past.
s0041.idiomatic: King Ling of Chu was conversing with Right Intendant Zige when Left Historiographer Yi Xiang hurried past.

s0042.literal: The king said, "This is a fine historiographer; he can read the Three Fu, Five Canons, Eight Suo, and Nine Mounds."
s0042.idiomatic: The king said, "This is a fine historiographer; he can read the Three Fu, Five Canons, Eight Suo, and Nine Mounds."

s0043.literal: Thus the historiographers of the feudal lords were not a single person each; all recorded words and events, and the Grand Historiographer gathered and adjudicated them to form the canonical records of the state.
s0043.idiomatic: Thus the historiographers of the feudal lords were not a single person each; all recorded words and events, and the Grand Historiographer gathered and adjudicated them to form the canonical records of the state.

s0044.literal: They did not embellish with false praise, nor conceal evil; thus censure and encouragement could take effect, and surviving texts remain worth reading—such as when the Zuo Commentary cites the Records of Zhou, and the Discourses of the States contains the Records of Zheng.
s0044.idiomatic: They did not embellish with false praise, nor conceal evil; thus censure and encouragement could take effect, and surviving texts remain worth reading—such as when the Zuo Commentary cites the Records of Zhou, and the Discourses of the States contains the Records of Zheng.

s0045.literal: When the Zhou royal house's Way declined, its fundamental norms fell into disorder, states differed in policy and families differed in custom, praise and blame lost their truth, and old regulations were overturned and confused.
s0045.idiomatic: When the Zhou royal house's Way declined, its fundamental norms fell into disorder, states differed in policy and families differed in custom, praise and blame lost their truth, and old regulations were overturned and confused.

s0046.literal: Confucius, with the talent of a great sage, in an age of collapse, lamented that the phoenix had not come and feared that this culture was about to fall, and so expounded the Way of the Changes, edited the Odes and Documents, revised the Spring and Autumn, and corrected the Major and Minor Odes.
s0046.idiomatic: Confucius, with the talent of a great sage, in an age of collapse, lamented that the phoenix had not come and feared that this culture was about to fall. He expounded the Way of the Changes, edited the Odes and Documents, revised the Spring and Autumn, and corrected the Major and Minor Odes.

s0047.literal: Where rites were broken and music collapsed, all were restored to their proper places.
s0047.idiomatic: Where rites were broken and music collapsed, all were restored to their proper places.

s0048.literal: From the time the wise man withered away and subtle words ceased, the seventy disciples scattered and the great meaning went astray; in the Warring States era the vertical and horizontal alliances flourished, truth and falsehood could not be distinguished, and the words of the various masters became confused and jumbled.
s0048.idiomatic: From the time the wise man withered away and subtle words ceased, the seventy disciples scattered and the great meaning went astray. In the Warring States era the vertical and horizontal alliances flourished, truth and falsehood could not be distinguished, and the words of the various masters became confused and jumbled.

s0049.literal: The utmost virtue of the sage was lost; the essential Way of the earlier kings perished.
s0049.idiomatic: The utmost virtue of the sage was lost; the essential Way of the earlier kings perished.

s0050.literal: Decline, confusion, and contradiction continued until the Qin.
s0050.idiomatic: Decline, confusion, and contradiction continued until the Qin.

s0051.literal: The Qin government roused the heart of wolf and jackal, erased the traces of earlier generations, burned the Odes and Documents, buried the scholars alive, made scribes its teachers, and issued the law against keeping books.
s0051.idiomatic: The Qin government roused the heart of wolf and jackal, erased the traces of earlier generations, burned the Odes and Documents, buried the scholars alive, made scribes its teachers, and issued the law against keeping books.

s0052.literal: Scholars fled in hardship, hiding in mountains and forests, or lost the original classics and passed them on by word of mouth.
s0052.idiomatic: Scholars fled in hardship, hiding in mountains and forests, or lost the original classics and passed them on by word of mouth.

s0053.literal: The Han dynasty destroyed Qin and Xiang Yu, and before even stepping down from the chariot, first ordered Shu Sun Tong to draft the rites of the cotton-mat altar, to remedy the evil of striking the pillar.
s0053.idiomatic: The Han dynasty destroyed Qin and Xiang Yu, and before even stepping down from the chariot, first ordered Shu Sun Tong to draft the rites of the cotton-mat altar, to remedy the evil of striking the pillar.

s0054.literal: Afterward Zhang Cang regulated the calendar, Lu Jia composed the New Discourses, Cao Shen recommended Lord Gai's teachings on Yellow Emperor and Laozi, Emperor Hui abolished the law against keeping books, and Confucian scholars at last practiced their craft among the people.
s0054.idiomatic: Afterward Zhang Cang regulated the calendar, Lu Jia composed the New Discourses, Cao Shen recommended Lord Gai's teachings on the Yellow Emperor and Laozi, Emperor Hui abolished the law against keeping books, and Confucian scholars at last practiced their craft among the people.

s0055.literal: Yet because the sage was already far removed, the classics and records were scattered and lost, bamboo slips were confused, and transmitted accounts were erroneous, so that the Documents came to be divided into two versions, the Odes into three, the Analects had Qi and Lu variants, and the Spring and Autumn had several schools of transmission.
s0055.idiomatic: Yet because the sage was already far removed, the classics and records were scattered and lost, bamboo slips were confused, and transmitted accounts were erroneous, so that the Documents came to be divided into two versions, the Odes into three, the Analects had Qi and Lu variants, and the Spring and Autumn had several schools of transmission.

s0056.literal: The rest contradicted one another in ways too numerous to recount.
s0056.idiomatic: The rest contradicted one another in ways too numerous to recount.

s0057.literal: This is why their learning was broad yet lacked essentials, laborious yet yielded little result.
s0057.idiomatic: This is why their learning was broad yet lacked essentials, laborious yet yielded little result.

s0058.literal: Emperor Wu established the Grand Historiographer, ordered that reports from throughout the realm be sent first to the Grand Historiographer and a copy to the Chancellor, opened the path for presenting books, established offices for copying books, and had external repositories in the Grand Sacrificer, Grand Historiographer, and Erudite, and internal repositories in the Extended Pavilion, Broad Inner Hall, and Secret Chamber.
s0058.idiomatic: Emperor Wu established the Grand Historiographer, ordered that reports from throughout the realm be sent first to the Grand Historiographer and a copy to the Chancellor, opened the path for presenting books, established offices for copying books, and had external repositories in the Grand Sacrificer, Grand Historiographer, and Erudite, and internal repositories in the Extended Pavilion, Broad Inner Hall, and Secret Chamber.

s0059.literal: Sima Tan and his son, for generations holding the post of Grand Historiographer, gathered materials from earlier ages, beginning from the Yellow Emperor down to Emperor Wu, and composed the Records in one hundred thirty chapters.
s0059.idiomatic: Sima Tan and his son, for generations holding the post of Grand Historiographer, gathered materials from earlier ages, beginning from the Yellow Emperor down to Emperor Wu, and composed the Records in one hundred thirty chapters.

s0060.literal: Examining its ritual system, it was largely the old practice of the historiographers.
s0060.idiomatic: Examining its ritual system, it was largely the old practice of the historiographers.

s0061.literal: By the time of Emperor Cheng, many books in the secret repository had been lost and scattered, so he sent Attendant Chen Nong to seek lost books throughout the realm.
s0061.idiomatic: By the time of Emperor Cheng, many books in the secret repository had been lost and scattered, so he sent Attendant Chen Nong to seek lost books throughout the realm.

s0062.literal: He ordered Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Xiang to collate the classics, commentaries, various masters, odes, and rhapsodies; Commandant of Footsoldiers Ren Hong to collate military books; Grand Historiographer Yin Xian to collate numerology; and Director of the Imperial Physicians Li Zhuguo to collate technical arts.
s0062.idiomatic: He ordered Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Xiang to collate the classics, commentaries, various masters, odes, and rhapsodies; Commandant of Footsoldiers Ren Hong to collate military books; Grand Historiographer Yin Xian to collate numerology; and Director of the Imperial Physicians Li Zhuguo to collate technical arts.

s0063.literal: Whenever a book was finished, Xiang would compose a record for it, discussing its purport, distinguishing its errors, arranging it, and submitting it to the throne.
s0063.idiomatic: Whenever a book was finished, Xiang would compose a record for it, discussing its purport, distinguishing its errors, arranging it, and submitting it to the throne.

s0064.literal: After Xiang died, Emperor Ai had his son Xin succeed to his father's work.
s0064.idiomatic: After Xiang died, Emperor Ai had his son Xin succeed to his father's work.

s0065.literal: He then moved the palace library books from the Green Chamber to the upper level of the Hall of Heavenly Blessings.
s0065.idiomatic: He then moved the palace library books from the Green Chamber to the upper level of the Hall of Heavenly Blessings.

s0066.literal: Xin then gathered all the texts together, extracted their essentials, and compiled the Seven Summaries: first, the General Summary; second, the Summary of the Six Arts; third, the Summary of the Various Masters; fourth, the Summary of Odes and Rhapsodies; fifth, the Summary of Military Books; sixth, the Summary of Numerology; seventh, the Summary of Technical Arts.
s0066.idiomatic: Xin then gathered all the texts together, extracted their essentials, and compiled the Seven Summaries: first, the General Summary; second, the Summary of the Six Arts; third, the Summary of the Various Masters; fourth, the Summary of Odes and Rhapsodies; fifth, the Summary of Military Books; sixth, the Summary of Numerology; seventh, the Summary of Technical Arts.

s0067.literal: In all, thirty-three thousand ninety scrolls.
s0067.idiomatic: In all, thirty-three thousand ninety scrolls.

s0068.literal: At the end of Wang Mang's reign, they were burned again.
s0068.idiomatic: At the end of Wang Mang's reign, they were burned again.

s0069.literal: When Emperor Guangwu restored the dynasty, he deeply loved refined culture, and Emperors Ming and Zhang followed his course, especially honoring classical learning.
s0069.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangwu restored the dynasty, he deeply loved refined culture, and Emperors Ming and Zhang followed his course, especially honoring classical learning.

s0070.literal: Great scholars from the four quarters, bearing their bundles and coming from afar, were beyond counting.
s0070.idiomatic: Great scholars from the four quarters, bearing their bundles and coming from afar, were beyond counting.

s0071.literal: The Stone Chamber and Orchid Terrace became ever more filled.
s0071.idiomatic: The Stone Chamber and Orchid Terrace became ever more filled.

s0072.literal: They also gathered new books at the Eastern Pavilion and the Hall of Benevolent Longevity, with Collators Ban Gu, Fu Yi, and others in charge.
s0072.idiomatic: They also gathered new books at the Eastern Pavilion and the Hall of Benevolent Longevity, with Collators Ban Gu, Fu Yi, and others in charge.

s0073.literal: They all followed the Seven Summaries in arranging book categories, and Gu further compiled them into the Bibliographic Treatise of the Book of Han.
s0073.idiomatic: They all followed the Seven Summaries in arranging book categories, and Gu further compiled them into the Bibliographic Treatise of the Book of Han.

s0074.literal: In the turmoil of Dong Zhuo, when Emperor Xian moved west, the books and silk scrolls were all taken by soldiers for curtains and bags.
s0074.idiomatic: In the turmoil of Dong Zhuo, when Emperor Xian moved west, the books and silk scrolls were all taken by soldiers for curtains and bags.

s0075.literal: What was collected and taken west still amounted to more than seventy cartloads.
s0075.idiomatic: What was collected and taken west still amounted to more than seventy cartloads.

s0076.literal: In the great chaos of the two capitals, everything was swept away and lost.
s0076.idiomatic: In the great chaos of the two capitals, everything was swept away and lost.

s0077.literal: When the Wei replaced the Han, they gathered what had been lost and stored it in the inner and outer three pavilions of the Secretariat.
s0077.idiomatic: When the Wei replaced the Han, they gathered what had been lost and stored it in the inner and outer three pavilions of the Secretariat.

s0078.literal: Secretariat Gentleman Zheng Mo of Wei first compiled the Inner Canon; Superintendent of the Secretariat Xun Xu then built on the Inner Canon and further compiled the New Register, dividing books into four sections and gathering all texts together.
s0078.idiomatic: Secretariat Gentleman Zheng Mo of Wei first compiled the Inner Canon; Superintendent of the Secretariat Xun Xu then built on the Inner Canon and further compiled the New Register, dividing books into four sections and gathering all texts together.

s0079.literal: The first was Section A, recording the Six Arts and elementary learning and the like;
s0079.idiomatic: The first was Section A, recording the Six Arts and elementary learning and the like;

s0080.literal: the second was Section B, containing ancient schools of the various masters, recent schools of the various masters, military books, military schools, and numerology;
s0080.idiomatic: the second was Section B, containing ancient schools of the various masters, recent schools of the various masters, military books, military schools, and numerology;

s0081.literal: the third was Section C, containing historical records, old affairs, the Imperial Overview Register, and miscellaneous matters;
s0081.idiomatic: the third was Section C, containing historical records, old affairs, the Imperial Overview Register, and miscellaneous matters;

s0082.literal: the fourth was Section D, containing odes and rhapsodies, illustrated encomia, and the Ji Tomb books.
s0082.idiomatic: the fourth was Section D, containing odes and rhapsodies, illustrated encomia, and the Ji Tomb books.

s0083.literal: In all, the four sections combined totaled twenty-nine thousand nine hundred forty-five scrolls.
s0083.idiomatic: In all, the four sections combined totaled twenty-nine thousand nine hundred forty-five scrolls.

s0084.literal: They only recorded titles and summaries, storing them in blue silk bags and writing on red silk.
s0084.idiomatic: They only recorded titles and summaries, storing them in blue silk bags and writing on red silk.

s0085.literal: As for the authors' intentions, there was no discussion or analysis.
s0085.idiomatic: As for the authors' intentions, there was no discussion or analysis.

s0086.literal: In the turmoil of the reigns of Emperor Hui and Emperor Huai, the capital was overturned and destroyed, and not a single text in the canal-pavilion archives survived.
s0086.idiomatic: In the turmoil of the reigns of Emperor Hui and Emperor Huai, the capital was overturned and destroyed, and not a single text in the canal-pavilion archives survived.

s0087.literal: At the beginning of Eastern Jin, they gradually gathered and reassembled books again.
s0087.idiomatic: At the beginning of Eastern Jin, they gradually gathered and reassembled books again.

s0088.literal: Director of Composition Li Chong collated them against Xu's old register; of what survived, there were only three thousand fourteen scrolls.
s0088.idiomatic: Director of Composition Li Chong collated them against Xu's old register; of what survived, there were only three thousand fourteen scrolls.

s0089.literal: Chong then gathered together the names of all the texts, arranging them only by sections A and B.
s0089.idiomatic: Chong then gathered together the names of all the texts, arranging them only by sections A and B.

s0090.literal: From then on this practice continued without change.
s0090.idiomatic: From then on this practice continued without change.

s0091.literal: Afterward books from the central court gradually flowed to the lands south of the Yangzi.
s0091.idiomatic: Afterward books from the central court gradually flowed to the lands south of the Yangzi.

s0092.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanjia of the Liu Song, Superintendent of the Secretariat Xie Lingyun compiled the Four-Section Catalog; in all, sixty-four thousand five hundred eighty-two scrolls.
s0092.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yuanjia of the Liu Song, Superintendent of the Secretariat Xie Lingyun compiled the Four-Section Catalog; in all, sixty-four thousand five hundred eighty-two scrolls.

s0093.literal: Secretariat Assistant Wang Jian also compiled a Catalog; in all, fifteen thousand seven hundred four scrolls.
s0093.idiomatic: Secretariat Assistant Wang Jian also compiled a Catalog; in all, fifteen thousand seven hundred four scrolls.

s0094.literal: Jian also separately compiled the Seven Records: first, the Record of Classics, recording the Six Arts, elementary learning, historical records, and miscellaneous biographies;
s0094.idiomatic: Jian also separately compiled the Seven Records: first, the Record of Classics, recording the Six Arts, elementary learning, historical records, and miscellaneous biographies;

s0095.literal: second, the Record of the Various Masters, recording ancient and modern various masters;
s0095.idiomatic: second, the Record of the Various Masters, recording ancient and modern various masters;

s0096.literal: third, the Record of Literary Writings, recording odes and rhapsodies;
s0096.idiomatic: third, the Record of Literary Writings, recording odes and rhapsodies;

s0097.literal: fourth, the Record of Military Books, recording military books;
s0097.idiomatic: fourth, the Record of Military Books, recording military books;

s0098.literal: fifth, the Record of Yin and Yang, recording yin-yang charts and weft texts;
s0098.idiomatic: fifth, the Record of Yin and Yang, recording yin-yang charts and weft texts;

s0099.literal: sixth, the Record of Technical Arts, recording technical skills;
s0099.idiomatic: sixth, the Record of Technical Arts, recording technical skills;

s0100.literal: seventh, the Record of Charts and Registers, recording territories and books.
s0100.idiomatic: seventh, the Record of Charts and Registers, recording territories and books.
